summary: Clarify how traffic-steering and partial pinning interact with data residency and observed latency variance
description: Customer asks for an explanation of why a subset of inference requests routed through cross-region traffic-steering still appear in audit logs as handled in the non-pinned region, and why those requests have 20-150ms additional latency compared to strictly pinned requests. They say they enabled partial pinning (pinning only for inference[:generate]) and a best-effort traffic-steering policy for embeddings. They want to ensure no customer PII leaves EU while keeping cost/latency tradeoffs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer account 'novahealth-prod' has strict_residency_policy=false and route-level override that pins inference.generate to eu-west. 2) From an EU-based test client, send 200 requests to /v1/generate and 200 requests to /v1/embeddings over 30 minutes. 3) Observe X-Redwood-Route and X-Redwood-Region headers, capture traces (trace IDs), and compare latency percentiles in Console. 4) Check audit log entries for request.region and request.backup_region fields and search routing decision logs for trace IDs.
expected_behavior: All requests for inference.generate should be handled in eu-west and audit logs should reflect eu-west as the final serving region; latency should align with eu-west SLOs and show no cross-region hop.
actual_behavior: Approximately 12% of inference.generate requests were served from us-east despite the pin rule; audit logs show request.origin_region=eu-west but serving_region=us-east for these traces. Those requests show an added 20-150ms tail latency compared to eu-west-served requests. Embeddings traffic used best-effort steering and occasionally fell back to us-east as expected.
logs: Example trace IDs: trace-20260310-01, trace-20260310-18, trace-20260310-22. Sample audit log line: "timestamp=2026-03-10T14:23:11Z account=novahealth-prod request_id=trace-20260310-18 origin_region=eu-west route=inference.generate pin_policy=partial serving_region=us-east routing_decision=failover_variant(reason=capacity_shortage)". Console screenshot link: https://console.redwood.ai/org/novahealth-prod/traffic/trace-20260310-18 (customer provided).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: pin rule applied at routing policy layer, but downstream capacity constraints caused automatic fallback to compatible variant in us-east. Review of autoscaling events for eu-west GPUs shows two brief scale-up delays (2026-03-10T14:20 and 2026-03-10T14:40) where available slots dipped below threshold; fallback policy kicked in. Routing logs show 'pin_violation' flagged when backend capacity < 2x request concurrency for pinned route. Also found that cache warmup for KV/prefix is per-region; requests handled in us-east missed EU-local cache and therefore incurred additional deserialization and remote KV fetch latency (~30-120ms observed).
comments:
[Support - Maya Chen 2026-03-10]: Acknowledge receipt and requested traces + policy config.
[Customer - Priya Rao 2026-03-10]: Uploaded traces and console link. Concerned about data sovereignty — asking if fallbacks can be disabled.
[SRE - Ravi Patel 2026-03-11]: Confirmed brief autoscaler lag in eu-west; fallback is expected behavior under failover policy. Noted pin policy type is partial which allows model variant fallback. Suggested two mitigation options.
[Support - Maya Chen 2026-03-11]: Provided mitigation suggestions and asked customer to confirm desired tradeoff (latency/cost vs strict residency).
resolution: Workaround provided: 1) Change the route-level pin policy from 'partial' to 'strict' to enforce hard residency (note: will queue/reject when eu-west capacity insufficient). 2) Add a proactive reserved capacity bump for eu-west Dedicated pool or enable faster autoscale thresholds to avoid brief capacity shortages. 3) Optionally enable cross-region KV replication for model caches to reduce cold-hop latency (requires configuration and may increase replication egress costs). Follow-up: SRE to open INT ticket to evaluate autoscaler tuning for short-lived spikes. Customer chose to switch to strict for inference.generate and request a Dedicated capacity review.
